title: Security and Governance for AI Solutions
objective: Explain how to protect data, access, outputs, and audits, and how to apply least privilege and continuous controls.

sections.title: Separate authentication, authorization, retrieval, and model invocation
paragraphs: Authentication verifies the identity of a user or service, while authorization determines which operations are permitted and what data they may access. Grant the application's IAM role only the operations it uses in Bedrock. When retrieving documents for RAG, the application verifies the logged-in user's permissions and limits the search to documents the user is authorized to access. Guardrails inspect the content of inputs sent to and outputs returned by the model.

sections.title: Protect data throughout input, storage, and output
paragraphs: Handle user inputs, retrieved documents, logs, and generated responses separately, and do not include more personal information or trade secrets in prompts than necessary. Include protection during storage and transmission, retention periods, deletion, and checks for sensitive information in outputs as requirements.

sections.title: Connecting Policies, Changes, and Audits
paragraphs: Governance is the framework used to define and verify the models and data that may be used, approved use cases, responsible owners, evaluation criteria, and exception handling. It records configuration changes, evaluations, access, and incident response, and continuously reviews policies against actual usage.

checkpoints.prompt: An internal information management officer needs a search application that handles confidential documents to investigate who attempted to access a document, when, and whether access was allowed. Auditors will review the records, but the document contents and users’ questions do not need to be retained in the audit logs. Choose one appropriate logging method.

choices.text: Continuously log the model’s inputs and outputs, and save the contents of every document included in the search.
choices.explanation: The document contents are not part of the audit requirements. Recording the original content broadens the scope of confidential information disclosed to log viewers.

choices.text: Record the executor’s identifier, document ID, time, and whether access was allowed or denied, and restrict log access to auditors.
choices.explanation: This tracks who attempted to access which document and when without storing the document contents or questions.

choices.text: Record only the model’s average response time and monthly cost.
choices.explanation: Aggregated time and cost data cannot be used to investigate individual document access.

choices.text: Record the number of successful operations by day only when the answer is displayed successfully.
choices.explanation: Success counts alone do not reveal the executor or the document for which access was attempted, and they cannot identify denied operations.

checkpoints.prompt: A developer at an insurance company is designing an AI that summarizes customer consultations. Which action at the input stage minimizes the handling of personal information?

choices.text: Include all information in the prompt, including unnecessary information.
Select the necessary information and define protection requirements for storage, output, and access.
choices.explanation: This protects the information throughout its lifecycle.

choices.text: Do not check the data policy or retention period.
choices.explanation: Using the data does not eliminate your responsibility.

checkpoints.prompt: Governance personnel want to trace the cause of quality degradation after changes to the model and prompts. Which operational practice is appropriate?

choices.text: Record the settings, approvals, evaluations, and access before and after changes, and review them regularly.
choices.explanation: This enables problems to be traced and controls to be verified.
Comparison and investigation of the cause are not possible.

choices.text: Perform quality evaluations only at the time of the initial release.
choices.explanation: This cannot address usage patterns or changes.

checkpoints.prompt: The medical guidance app development team wants to reject harmful inputs and avoid displaying responses that contain sensitive information. How should content review and access control for AWS resources be divided? Select one.

choices.text: Manage users’ AWS permissions using Guardrails alone.
choices.explanation: Guardrails does not replace IAM authorization.

choices.text: Control invocation permissions with IAM, evaluate input and output policies with Guardrails, and validate the configuration.
choices.explanation: Operate authorization and content controls separately.

choices.text: Use IAM alone to determine whether text is harmful.
Remove the controls if the response sounds natural.
choices.explanation: Natural phrasing does not guarantee safety.

checkpoints.prompt: The designer of an internal RAG system wants to prevent authenticated regular employees from retrieving accounting documents. Which measure is most appropriate?

choices.text: Return all documents if the user is authenticated.
choices.explanation: Authentication verifies the user’s identity. Authorization determines which data the user can access.

choices.text: Use role-based authorization to apply least privilege to the search scope and Bedrock calls.
choices.explanation: Authorization controls which data and operations are permitted.
This does not provide access control.

choices.text: Determine document-viewing permissions solely with Guardrails.
choices.explanation: Content control is not a substitute for authorization.
